assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the vault design and the final assessment.

faq.q: Does the platform run my Solidity or tests?
faq.a: No. The labs check your design, analysis and calculations. You run the code in your own tools, and the lessons show what to run.
You should be comfortable with basic Solidity and the Ethereum model, for example from the earlier courses in this series.

faq.q: Will it make my contracts safe?
faq.a: It teaches habits that reduce risk. Contracts holding real value still need professional audits, legal advice and ongoing monitoring.

activities.title: How much does packing save?
activities.objective: Calculate storage slots and the gas saved when related variables share a slot.
activities.scenario: Writing a variable into a fresh storage slot costs about 22,100 gas. Two uint128 values can share one 32-byte slot if they sit next to each other. Compare the Unpacked and Packed layouts. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B6 work out the slots used by the unpacked layout: 3.
In B7 work out the slots used by the packed layout: 2.
In B8 work out the first-write gas for the unpacked layout: slots times the gas per new slot (B2).
In B9 work out the first-write gas for the packed layout.
In B10 work out the gas saved by packing: B8 minus B9.
In B11 work out the saving over the number of contracts deployed in a year (B3): B10 times B3.
In B12 convert the yearly saving to ETH at the gas price in B4 (gwei): B11 times B4 divided by 1,000,000,000.

checks.label: B8 is the unpacked gas
checks.explain: Slots times the gas per slot.

checks.label: B9 is the packed gas
B10 is the gas saved
B11 is the yearly saving
checks.explain: Saving per write times the number of writes.

checks.label: B12 is the saving in ETH
checks.explain: Gas times gwei, converted to ETH.

cells.A2: Gas for writing a new slot
cells.A3: Contracts or structs written per year

activities.title: Who pays for a gasless transaction?
activities.objective: Model the cost of a service that pays gas for users using signed messages.
activities.scenario: A game lets players sign actions off-chain and a relayer submits them in batches. Compare the cost with players sending their own transactions. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In B7 work out the cost if every action is its own transaction: actions times the gas for one transaction, times the gas price.
In B8 work out the cost when the relayer batches actions: batches times the gas for a batch (B4), plus the extra gas per action (B5) times actions, times the gas price.
In B9 work out how many actions fit in one batch: the batch limit (B6) divided by the extra gas per action, rounded down with INT.
In B10 work out the saving: B7 minus B8.
In B11 show Worth it if the saving is above zero, else Not worth it.

checks.label: B7 is the separate cost
B8 is the batched cost
B9 is the actions per batch
checks.hint: =INT(B6/B5)
checks.explain: The limit divided by the per-action gas.

checks.label: B10 is the gas saved
B11 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(B10>0,"Worth it","Not worth it")
checks.explain: A positive saving is worth it.

cells.A4: Gas overhead of one batch transaction
cells.A5: Extra gas per action inside a batch
cells.A9: Actions that fit in one batch

activities.title: Read a gas report and decide
activities.objective: Compare gas before and after an optimisation and decide whether it pays for the extra complexity.
activities.scenario: A gas report shows the cost of three functions before and after optimisation. Each is called a different number of times per month. Work out the saving and the cost in rupees. (Teaching figures.)
steps: In E2 work out the gas saved per call: before minus after. Fill down to E4.
In F2 work out the gas saved per month: saved per call times calls. Fill down.
In F6 total the monthly saving.
In F7 convert to rupees using the gas price in B8 (gwei) and the ETH price in B9.
In F8 show Worth the effort if the monthly saving is above the engineer's cost of the change in B10, otherwise Skip it.

checks.label: E2 is the saving per deposit
F2 is the monthly saving for deposit
F6 is the total saving
checks.hint: =SUM(F2:F4)

checks.label: F7 is the value in rupees
F8 is the verdict
checks.hint: =IF(F7>B10,"Worth the effort","Skip it")

Under Threats list at least four risks in bullets.
Keep it between 320 and 640 words.
